prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE exceptionally polished desktop website design comp, 1536x1024 landscape: the homepage first viewport plus the beginning of the next section. A real web layout, edge to edge, no device frame and no browser chrome. Brand: Birdcar, the consulting practice of Nick Cannariato, one Silicon Valley systems engineer who builds purpose-built tools and workflows for established service businesses, so their teams do better work faster and the business can grow without hiring another coordinator. Visual world: the client's own business as a living miniature, a crisp premium 3D isometric diorama rendered like a high-end architectural product render: soft studio daylight, matte stone, pale wood, teal-cyan floor tiles, fine detail, small realistic figures, never a cartoon. Navigation about 80px on a pale daylight ground (#eef3f1): at left the wordmark "Birdcar" in a forward-leaning mid-century connected brush script (Alkaline style), ink #122127; at right the links "How I work", "Selected work", "Writing", and a compact canary-yellow (#f5c542) button "Book a free Walkthrough →" with ink text and 6px radius.

STRUCTURE, in reading order:
1. The navigation described above.
2. LEFT (x 40 to 960, y 100 to 860): a large isometric diorama of a small service business (front desk, open office with desks and small figures, a shop bay with a white van and shelving, and a glass-walled owner's office at the back), shown mid-transformation and divided by a thin vertical slider line with a round canary-yellow grab handle at its middle. LEFT of the line, labeled by a small pill "Today": thin dotted paths from every desk tangle toward the owner's glass office, where a tall teetering paper stack sits under a red warning light and small glowing yellow cubes pile up; a canary sits inside a closed brass cage. RIGHT of the line, labeled by a small pill "After the fix": the same building, calm: cubes flow along clean straight illuminated teal lanes directly between desks and a shared wall screen, the owner's desk is clear with a coffee cup, the warning light is off, and the cage door is open with the canary perched on the desk lamp. Beneath the diorama, a small hint with a two-way arrow: "Drag to compare".
3. RIGHT column (x 1000 to 1460, y 180 to 700): headline in a warm confident grotesk, ink #122127, about 64px, three lines: "Why does everything come back to you?" A subline at about 19px: "I build tools around how your team actually works, so they do better work, faster, and the business can grow without another hire." A canary-yellow button "Book a free Walkthrough →", and beneath it small text: "One pitch-free hour. A written report within three business days. Yours to keep."
4. A white bottom band (y 890 to 1024): a small line "Where I've built systems" and a row of typographic wordmarks: GitHub, Heroku, Zapier, Twilio, Salesforce.

ART DIRECTION: one dominant move, the miniature business; everything else calm and legible. Refined, adult, premium render with precise lighting; not cute, no toy proportions, no clay blobs. Every wall sign, poster, van panel, and doormat in the scene is blank: no invented words or slogans anywhere in the diorama except the listed label tags. Past-employer names are plain typographic wordmarks only, no logo icons. No purple, no gradient orbs, no AI imagery, no robots, no stock photos, no fake metrics or testimonials. Spell every quoted word exactly, including "Walkthrough". Treat it as a finished, shippable website.
